summary:
EVERY COMMAND h_oracle QUOTED WAS RE-RUN ON THE TREE AS IT IS AND EVERY ONE OF THEM PRINTED WHAT THEY SAID IT PRINTED. That is unusual for this repository and I want it said first: 13 of 13 guard-deletion behaviours, the 20-of-34 / 0-of-34 sweep with the survivor list matching line for line, the three aee4a52 measurements, the two N8 escapes, and the before-case-count 381 all reproduce EXACTLY. Note the tree has MOVED since h_oracle wrote: HEAD is now d57bdc0, their work and every sibling's is committed, the working tree is clean, and THE WHOLE SUITE IS GREEN -- ownership 13+33 0 failing; contract 15+66 0 (K15 now PASSes: a sibling rendered the value at src/opt/api.py:1930 in d57bdc0, so h_oracle's 'one failure I am leaving red' is closed and was correctly attributed); census 8 0 with 26 self-test cases; assemble 9 0; couplings 4 0; fabric 8 0; derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches.

NO NARROWING. I checked the charge directly rather than accepting the paragraph. `git diff de76093 HEAD -- tests/test_derive.py tests/test_census.py | grep '^-[^-]'` is 37 lines and I read all 37: 5 are docstring prose, 18 are `try:`/`except UnitError:`/`pass` scaffolding that reappears as `except UnitError as e:` plus an assertion naming the arm, and the remaining 14 are four value assertions, one loop header and one try-block -- every one of which reappears in the rewritten block carrying the SAME expected value plus more (1024x1, 1024x64, Windows(10), the foreign-kind tuple, the zero divisor, the Clock-rate case for run_windows_from_epochs). Not one assertion, case or check was weakened or removed. The two new N8 arms are additive and I proved each is individually load-bearing: reverting ONLY the broken-pointer arm fails exactly one new self-test case, reverting ONLY the empty-population arm fails exactly one other, and reverting both fails all three.

I ALSO RE-DERIVED THE NUMBERS RATHER THAN REPLAYING THEM. All eleven small opt_steps_from_windows rows and all five above 2**53 were computed in a separate process that never imports derive, and every one matches: 1087//64=16, 1088//64=17, 63//64=0 floored to 1, 2**53+3 = 2 x 4503599627370497 + 1, 2**54+2 = 2 x 9007199254740993. `int(n/w) != want` holds at all five, at deltas -1, +1, +1, -2, -1, so the discriminating row is real and not decorative. The case counts check out too: my tracer gives BEFORE 266 asserts + 115 refusals = 381, EXACTLY their number, and AFTER 443 + 205, where 5 of my 443 are one two-physical-line assert counted twice per iteration -- 438 + 205 = 643, their number to the unit. N8's population, counted independently off DEPARTURES, is six line-form entries carrying 1+2+2+3+1+1 = 10 spans and three prose entries: 10 / 6 / 3, what it prints.

ONE CLAIM OF THEIRS IS FALSE AND IT IS A CITATION. Finding 7 says they opened opt/api.py::build and it 'holds the function's two call sites at :566 and :754, both inside build'. src/opt/api.py:566 is INSIDE build's DOCSTRING (the docstring node spans 539-666); the AST finds exactly ONE Call to opt_steps_from_windows in that file, at :754. Their own repro could not have caught this -- it only asked whether the line number falls inside a FunctionDef, which a docstring line does. Nothing in the committed tree carries the wrong number, so the damage is confined to the report, but it is the 'open the file before you cite it' rule failing inside the paragraph that claims to have obeyed it.

THREE LIVE HOLES IN THEIR OWN FILE THAT NOBODY REPORTED, FOUND BY EXTENDING THEIR OWN METHOD. Their headline is '0 SURVIVORS OF 34', and it is exactly true -- I independently confirmed all 34 Raise nodes in src/spine/derive.py sit inside an `if`, so the sweep's population is complete FOR THAT SHAPE. But the shape is `if <test>: raise`, and derive.py's rules are not all raises. I ran the same discipline over the BODIES (21 single-token behaviour mutations, tests/test_derive.py re-run on each) and three survive with the suite green: (a) opt_steps_from_backwards' `Steps(n // k)` -> `Steps(int(n / k))` -- the substitution that function's own closing comment rejects BY NAME, and which h_oracle's new group (6) QUOTES as its authority while pinning only opt_steps_from_windows; it answers Steps(9007199254740992) for Backwards(2**53+1) at accum=1 and Steps(4503599627370498) at 2**53+3/accum=2, one optimizer step SHORT and one step LONG, and test_derive.py prints '575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches' and exits 0; (b) cadences_that_cannot_fire's `period.n <= 0` -> `== 0`, after which a NEGATIVE period vanishes from the audit entirely ([] instead of [('g', -500, 0)]) -- the precise regression the four-line comment above that arm records as already having happened once; (c) pin_tick's `dstep = max(Windows(0), Windows(dstep))`, deleted: a PINNED clock runs BACKWARDS, Windows(2650) with dstep Windows(-16) answering Windows(2634), and at Windows(-3000) answering Windows(-350) -- a pinned-at-cap clock reading negative. The 32 oracle cases carry dstep in {0, 1, 16, 100} and no negative, and no line of smoke() passes one.

AND N8 STILL HAS THE ESCAPE IT WAS REPAIRED FOR, IN THREE SPELLINGS. The repair reports a clause appended AFTER a citation. A clause placed BEFORE it is still counted as prose: I set one entry's `where` to 'see the note, src/fabric/levers.py:296-307' and N8 returned 0 and printed PASS -- '9 line span(s) opened across 5 departure(s); 4 point at prose'. Deleting the `where` key outright, or setting it to '', does the same. Applying it to all six DOES fail, because the new empty-population arm catches that, so the hole is bounded at 'any five of six, silently'. This is a residual, not a regression -- the check is strictly stronger than it was -- and the docstring does declare the rule it enforces, but 'A data table is not allowed to switch a check off' is not yet true for one entry at a time.

I PLANTED EVERY SHAPE N8 CLAIMS AND A LOOKALIKE. Drifted span -> FAIL; span off the end -> FAIL; missing file -> FAIL; broken pointer -> FAIL; whole table reduced to prose -> FAIL; untouched tree -> PASS; the abstention case (a `where` with no colon) -> PASS. One lookalike now fails that did not before: a prose `where` written with a colon, 'spine/assemble.py: the DOM row', is reported as a broken pointer. No live entry has that shape and the docstring states the rule, so it is a declared trade-off rather than a false positive -- but it is a new way for a correct-looking citation to be called wrong, and it is worth knowing before someone edits the table.

GATES: none. Neither owned file constructs a Gate (`grep -c 'Gate(' ` is 0 in both), so there is no cell of the lever space to sweep for a self-contradicting sentence in their scope. What their assertions now BLESS is refusal prose in a sibling's file, so I printed all 26 of those messages in full and read them. Twenty-five are consistent. One is not, and it is unreported: src/spine/derive.py:663-665 tells the caller 'It is batch_windows x accum, and both are floored at 1 by their own declarations' -- opt/levers.py:274 says in as many words that 'a Lever has no range facility at all', :277-279 lists batch_windows=0 as refused only downstream and accum=0 as clamped only at accum_due's read site, and flush_period_windows' OWN message 300 lines earlier says 'spine/lever.py::Lever carries a default, a help string, a unit and choices and no bound ... which accepts a negative'. The floor is in spine/assemble.py:1149's Coupling compute, not in either declaration. h_oracle's new group (8) asserts the first clause of that sentence and so puts a test behind the paragraph containing the false one.
